answer: A refundable stake bonded to each identity works like a jetty charging every boat a deposit before it may dock. One fake agent is cheap, but ten thousand sockpuppets must each lock real capital, and one proven fraud burns the deposit, so attacker cost grows with every identity while honest agents face only a temporary lock. Aged reputation is a second anchor: a fresh account is a relic with no provenance and cannot outvote long-lived participants, just as a mesa stands only because its layers built up slowly. Together, stake plus history make mass forgery unprofitable.
